Images.Description: C5aR1+/CD11b+ cells correspond to immunosuppressive TAMs

Header: Complement activation on tumor cells correlated with increased infiltration of C5aR1+/CD11b+ tumor associated macrophages (TAMs). Their identity was further supported by single-nucleus RNA-seq data showing enrichment of C5AR1 and ITGAM/ITGB2 (CR3, CD11b/CD18) co-expression in TAMs.

Waypoints.Name: C5aR1+/CD11b+ macrophages
Waypoints.Description: C5aR1+/CD11b+/CD68+ macrophages preferentially localized near C3+/CA9+ malignant cells, revealing a close spatial relationship between complement-opsonized tumor cells and complement responsive macrophages.

Waypoints.Name: C5aR1+/CD11b+ macrophages and T cells
Waypoints.Description: C5aR1+/CD11b+ macrophages displayed a C1qTAM phenotype, characterized by C1q, MHC-II, and PD-L1 expression, and localized in close proximity to CTLA4+ T cells. These findings suggest a potential feed-forward loop in which local complement activation may favor the accumulation of complement-responsive macrophages that, in turn, could sustain CP activation through C1q production. Their high MHC-II expression poins to antigen-presenting capacity that may help sustain an immune-infiltrated, "hot" TME, while PD-L1 expression may simultaneously restrain local T-cell responses. This dual immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive phenotype may explain why C1qTAMs are associated with poor prognosis in localized disease, yet with improved response to immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic ccRCC.
